name: Gears of War 2 - Hollow
post_apply_message:
Gears of War 2 - Hollow (community PC port, UE3) — Apply adds the Steam shortcut on GE-Proton 10.34 pointing at Binaries/GoW2Hollow.exe and writes your display/camera/input settings.

WHY THE INI AND NOT THE LAUNCHER: the game has NO in-game options menu, and GoW2Hollow_Launcher.exe is a 64-bit PySide6 app that spawns the 32-bit game as a CHILD process — which breaks Steam's process tracking (Steam sees the game exit when the launcher does). The launcher is only a GUI over these same ini files, so the recipe writes them directly and the launcher is never needed on Linux. Unusually for UE3, Hollow REGENERATES GearEngine.ini / GearCamera.ini / GearInput.ini from the Default*.ini on every launch, so editing the Default* files is authoritative — there is no generated user config to chase.

SETTINGS: 1920x1200, fullscreen, 2x MSAA, 16x anisotropic, PoolSize 512, everything else as Tony had it. These are HANDHELD values — the Windows side has the launcher for its own settings, so this recipe exists for the machines that don't.

1920x1200 IS 16:10, WHICH IS THE POINT. Both the Legion Go 2 (1920x1200) and the Steam Deck (1280x800) are 16:10 panels, so this gives the correct aspect ratio on either — native on the Go 2, clean 1.5x supersampling on a Deck. The launcher only ever offers 16:9 and ultrawide presets, never 16:10, which is why this can't be set from its UI; the ini takes any integers and the port handles unusual aspect ratios fine (its own preset list runs to 5120x1440 / 32:9).

MSAA IS THE COST DRIVER, not the resolution — if it struggles, take MaxMultisamples to 1 (1 = off in UE3; there is no 0) before touching anything else. MaxAnisotropy at 16 is nearly free, so it stays. PoolSize=512 (up from the shipped 140) is the anti-pop-in / anti-streaming-hitch lever; don't push it much past this on a handheld, where the texture pool competes with system RAM rather than sitting in dedicated VRAM.

FRAME PACING: bSmoothFrameRate stays True with MaxSmoothedFrameRate=120 deliberately. UE3 clamps reported delta time into [1/Max, 1/Min] (Min=22 from BaseEngine.ini), so a 120 ceiling keeps the clamp boundary well clear of a 60 Hz frame time — setting Max=60 would put the boundary exactly on it. Cap to the display with SteamOS/gamescope instead. If a dip ever renders as SLOW MOTION rather than stutter, that's the Min=22 clamp: set bSmoothFrameRate=False.

DXVK: nothing to do. The dgVoodoo2 D3D9->D3D11 fix circulating for Windows exists to escape the legacy D3D9 driver path; Proton already replaces d3d9 with DXVK (D3D9 -> Vulkan), so stacking dgVoodoo would just add a second translation layer.
notes:
Built 2026-07-31 from Tony's copy at F:\Games\Gears of War 2 - Hollow (10.87 GB, 2600 files), staged to NAS _games/. UE3 fan port of a game never released on PC; not a cracked commercial title.

EXE: Binaries/GoW2Hollow.exe (36 MB, x86) — VERIFIED on disk, and note the case (capital B in Binaries, capital G in GearGame) after the Halo MCC lowercase-mcc/ mistake. GoW2Hollow_Launcher.exe and Uninstall.exe are the SAME 47.3 MB binary (identical MD5) — one PyInstaller/PySide6 exe branching on its own filename. start_dir is Binaries/ (exe dir, UE3 convention); if the game can't find its content, try {game_dir} instead — the launcher itself Popens the exe with the install root as cwd.

SETTINGS PROVENANCE: based on Tony's own launcher-configured settings read off F: on 2026-07-31 (NOT the shipped defaults, which were 1280x720, MaxMultisamples=1, MaxAnisotropy=4, MaxSmoothedFrameRate=60), then adjusted for a handheld per his instructions: Fullscreen False->True, MaxAnisotropy 8->16, MaxMultisamples 8->2, 3840x2160->1920x1200, PoolSize 140->512. Ran at 1920x1080 first and played well; moved to 1200 for the correct 16:10 aspect on Tony's request (+11% pixels). Bools are written as the strings 'True'/'False' rather than JSON booleans because ini_edit's _fmt turns JSON true into '1' — UE3 accepts 1, but matching the file's own spelling keeps it readable and diffable.

DELIBERATELY ONE SET OF VALUES. An earlier draft split these across a shared block plus a per-hostname override so one recipe could serve the desktop too; Tony correctly called that overbuilt — Windows has the launcher, so the recipe only needs to serve Linux. ini_edit still SUPPORTS values_by_host (built and tested at the same time) if a future recipe genuinely needs per-machine display values; this one doesn't use it.

Settings the launcher also exposes but the recipe leaves alone: keybinds (DefaultInput.ini [Engine.PlayerInput] Bindings array), camera shake ([GearGame.GearCamMod_CameraBone]), and the dedicated-server options ([GearGameContent.GearGame*] — Horde/TDM/Annex/CTM/KTL/Wingman). The launcher's own prefs (player name, extra_args, launch-via-Steam) live in launcher_config.json, which doesn't exist until the launcher is run; extra_args is redundant here since Steam launch options do the same job.

Non-Steam -> computed appid from the recipe id. UNTESTED on hardware.
